text:
ashley: Anyone else seeing edge-prod-us-east-2 model-serving pods flapping readiness? ALB target group shows 504s and a bunch of pods are "ready: false".
vikas: Yeah. I noticed infra-nacl changes earlier today — @infra-deploy-bot applied a rule set around 11:23. Could be related.
charlie: Symptoms look like reply-path blocked. ALB healthchecks are TCP/HTTP from ELB IPs, but NACLs are stateless. If ephemeral ports for return traffic are denied, health checks will fail even if SG allows them.
sam: Also seeing DNS timeouts inside pods: `nslookup model-store.s3-us-east-2.amazonaws.com` hangs for ~2s then fails. That might explain readiness probes that do external calls.
ashley: Paste from pod logs:
```
2026-03-17T11:35:02Z model-proxy: dial tcp 52.216.12.98:443: i/o timeout
2026-03-17T11:35:04Z model-proxy: lookup model-store.s3-us-east-2.amazonaws.com: no such host
```
net-bot: Detected NACL deny events for 10.0.0.0/16 -> 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 32768-65535 at 2026-03-17T11:23:10Z. Count: 1849. (cloudwatch-link)
vikas: That's the ephemeral port range. Someone hardened egress NACLs and forgot to add return rules for ephemeral ports. Because NACLs are evaluated both directions, you need allow rules for ephemeral ports in both inbound and outbound for the NAT/ELB flows.
charlie: Interesting twist: our nodes route outbound DNS to VPC resolver (10.0.0.2). The resolver replies source port 53 -> client ephemeral port. If ephemeral inbound is denied on NACL, DNS replies get dropped and everything looks like a DNS blackhole.
sam: Repro steps I ran from a node (host namespace):
```
curl -v --resolve model-store.s3-us-east-2.amazonaws.com:443:52.216.12.98 https://model-store.s3-us-east-2.amazonaws.com/health
* Connected to 52.216.12.98 (52.216.12.98) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake... then no application data -> timeout
```
ashley: Quick mitigation: can we allow ephemeral ports in NACL for the problematic subnet(s)? Proposed rules:
```
# inbound (from internet -> subnet)
Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 80,443 from 0.0.0.0/0
Rule 110: ALLOW TCP 32768-65535 from 0.0.0.0/0
# outbound (subnet -> internet)
Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 0-65535 to 0.0.0.0/0
```
vikas: I can patch NACL to add ephemeral allow on inbound for the private subnets that host GPU nodes. Doing it in 2 AZs now.
devops-bot: terraform apply started by vikas (plan id: tf-apply-4421) — changes: +2 aws_network_acl_rule
net-bot: Confirmed new NACL rule applied at 2026-03-17T11:41:05Z for subnet-abc123 (us-east-2a). Deny events dropped to 0 within 30s.
charlie: Healthchecks starting to pick up: ALB target group shows healthy -> 12/36 targets now healthy, latency normalizing.
ashley: DNS resolves again inside affected pods. Running a small smoke test across 20 pods — 19 passed, 1 still timed out but restarted and passed.
vikas: Root cause note for postmortem: applied restrictive NACL change intended to limit outbound ephemeral-to-internet, but forgot that stateless NACLs require symmetric ephemeral allowances for return traffic (including DNS replies and ALB source port replies). Also missed that NAT gateway responses will come from ephemeral ports.
sam: Follow-ups: 1) Add an automated NACL checker for ephemeral rules when footprinting ELB/NAT flows. 2) Add a runbook entry in eng-runtime for quick mitigation. 3) Add an integration test that verifies ALB healthcheck roundtrips after NACL changes.
ashley: Thanks all — :thumbsup: Deployed fix held. I'll file the postmortem and link infra-deploy PR.
devops-bot: PR https://git.company/repo/infra/pull/987 merged by vikas — rollforward applied.
charlie: Adding note: GPUs in us-east-2 were impacted but there was no data loss, just latency and readiness flaps. Marking incident SEV: low -> mid (briefly degraded capacity)
ashley: Closing thread once postmortem posted.
